# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 47

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 47:1 "given over" vs. "handed over" vs. "given specifically to"

- **EMET:** "given them over to you who are of the world"
- **LOGOS:** "handed them over to those of you who are in the world"
- **PNEUMA:** "I gave these commandments specifically to people like you"
- **Greek:** *paredōka hymin tois en tō kosmō ousi* — I handed over/gave to you who are in the world
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "handed them over to those of you who are in the world" (LOGOS). *Paradidōmi* (hand over/deliver) is a specific transmission verb; PNEUMA adds "specifically" not in the Greek.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 47:2 "makes known" vs. "make known"

- **EMET:** "I shall make known to you also the works of the devil's deeds"
- **LOGOS:** "I will also make known to you the workings of the devil"
- **PNEUMA:** "Let me also tell you about the devil's methods"
- **Greek:** *gnōrisō soi kai ta erga tou diabolou* — I will make known to you also the works of the devil
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "I will also make known to you the workings of the devil" (LOGOS). "Workings" better captures *erga* (works/operations) in context.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 47:2 "comes" vs. "approaches"

- **EMET:** "when the man who is righteous comes"
- **LOGOS:** "when a righteous man approaches"
- **PNEUMA:** "when a righteous person comes near"
- **Greek:** *hotan elthē ho anthrōpos ho dikaios* — when the righteous man comes
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when a righteous man approaches" (LOGOS). "Approaches" suggests proximity and encounter; "comes" is vaguer.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 47:2 "double-minded and weak" vs. "double-minded and faint-hearted"

- **EMET:** "the man who is double-minded and weak"
- **LOGOS:** "a double-minded and faint-hearted man"
- **PNEUMA:** "a double-minded, weak-willed person"
- **Greek:** *ho dipsychos kai ho deilos* — the double-minded and the cowardly/faint-hearted
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "a double-minded and faint-hearted man" (LOGOS). *Deilos* = cowardly/faint-hearted; not merely "weak" (EMET) or "weak-willed" (PNEUMA).

---

## Disagreement 5 — 47:3 "stands firm" vs. "is valiant"

- **EMET:** "the man who is full of faith is valiant against the devil"
- **LOGOS:** "the man who is full of faith stands firm against the devil"
- **PNEUMA:** "a faith-filled person stands firm against the devil"
- **Greek:** *dynatos estin kata tou diabolou* — is powerful/strong against the devil
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "stands firm against the devil." LOGOS and PNEUMA agree; "valiant" (EMET) is a strong but archaic word; "stands firm" captures the military stance better.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 47:3 "comes easily under his influence" vs. "falls under his influence without difficulty"

- **EMET:** "comes easily under his influence"
- **LOGOS:** "comes under his influence without difficulty"
- **PNEUMA:** "easily falls under his influence"
- **Greek:** *katakyrieuthēsetai hyp' autou* — he will be dominated/overcome by him
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "comes under his influence without difficulty" (LOGOS). The passive verb *katakyrieuthēsetai* suggests being overcome/dominated; "easily" (EMET/PNEUMA) is a reasonable paraphrase.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 47:4 "the Lord is the Angel of Righteousness"

- **EMET:** "the Lord is the Angel of Righteousness"
- **LOGOS:** "the Lord himself is the Angel of Righteousness"
- **PNEUMA:** "the Lord himself is the Angel of Righteousness"
- **Greek:** *ho kyrios estin ho angelos tēs dikaiosynēs* — the Lord is the angel of righteousness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the Lord is the Angel of Righteousness" (EMET). The identification is startling enough without adding "himself" (LOGOS/PNEUMA), which is not in the Greek text here.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 47:4 "strengthen" vs. "fortifies"

- **EMET:** "he strengthens all believers"
- **LOGOS:** "he fortifies all who have faith"
- **PNEUMA:** "He strengthens everyone who has faith"
- **Greek:** *krataioi tous... pisteuontas* — he makes strong/empowers those who believe
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "fortifies all who have faith" (LOGOS). *Krataiooō* = to make strong/fortify; "fortify" is more specific than the general "strengthen."

---

## Disagreement 9 — 47:5 "place to live and dwell" vs. "place and dwelling"

- **EMET:** "the devil has a place to live and dwell only among those who are double-minded"
- **LOGOS:** "the devil has place and dwelling only among those who are double-minded"
- **PNEUMA:** "the only people the devil has access to are the double-minded"
- **Greek:** *topon echei...kai katoikia* — he has a place/space and dwelling
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the devil has place and dwelling only among those who are double-minded" (LOGOS). The parallel *topos...katoikia* should be preserved; PNEUMA's paraphrase loses the spatial imagery.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 47:5 "cannot withstand" vs. "cannot stand"

- **EMET:** "the devil cannot withstand" (the faithful)
- **LOGOS:** "the devil cannot stand"
- **PNEUMA:** "he can't stand against people who have genuine faith"
- **Greek:** *ou dynastai antistēnai* — is not able to stand against/withstand
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the devil cannot stand" (LOGOS). "Cannot stand" is slightly stronger in English idiom; PNEUMA adds "genuine" not in the Greek.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 47.*
